summary: In structured Bayesian models, a large latent block is often Gaussian conditional on a smaller set of parameters, yet generic inference methods relearn this geometry during warmup. We study how this structure can be used to construct transports for posterior inference.
takeaways: We study how this structure can be used to construct transports for posterior inference.
Marginalization requires an identity established from the model; numerical evidence alone permits only a target-preserving change of variables, and a failed check leaves the model unchanged.
On the Stock-Watson inflation model, CONGA improves minimum ESS per second by 12.5x for NUTS.
